missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend calcium supplementation until stone type, total dietary calcium, kidney function and current products are clarified.
safety_exclusions: Do not assume all kidney stones are calcium stones.
Do not advise indiscriminate restriction of dietary calcium; appropriate dietary calcium can be important in some stone-prevention plans.
Do not infer a calcium deficiency from stone history.
professional_escalation_conditions: Recurrent stones, hypercalciuria, calcium phosphate stones, chronic kidney disease, hypercalcemia or current obstruction.
Severe flank pain with fever, vomiting or inability to urinate requires urgent assessment.
population_and_context: People with a history of kidney stones being assessed for calcium supplementation; stone composition, dietary calcium, urinary risk factors and existing products matter.
dose_constraints: No dose from this rule. Assess dietary calcium and stone-specific advice with a clinician; if supplementation is indicated, consider elemental calcium amount and timing.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Calcium fact sheet provides general intake and safety information; individualized stone prevention requires current urology/nephrology guidance and stone-specific evaluation.
